title: (No AI) AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
author: Richard Lawler
content:
![Graphic image of a data center.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/STKS528_DATA_CENTERS2_B.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Poll data released Tuesday [by the _New York Times_ and Siena University](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/15/us/politics/ai-polls-midterms.html) confirms what we've [already been seeing](https://www.theverge.com/policy/916210/ai-midterm-elections-data-centers-jobs), and [what politicians are responding to](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/983677/now-politicians-say-they-are-against-data-centers) - AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular. Asked if they support or oppose the construction of data centers to power AI tech, 61 percent of the 1,503 likely voters surveyed in early September (ahead of the recent [AI safety slowdown discussion](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/995186/is-big-techs-ai-slowdown-a-safety-pact-or-a-cartel)) said they were opposed, with only 14 percent saying they strongly support. The split was about even among 2024 Donald Trump voters, at 49 percent support to 45 percent oppose, while people who had voted for Kamala Harris or who didn't vote leaned opp …

title: (No AI) Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![Two visuals showing perks for Meta One Core and Premium plans](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Meta-One-Bundle-plans-for-individuals.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Shortly after launching its new do-everything [AI assistant Muse](https://www.theverge.com/tech/993391/meta-muse-ai-hands-on), Meta's launching subscription bundles that pair its standalone app subscriptions with extra AI usage. Some of the new [Meta One bundles](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-meta-one-subscription-service-more-features-ai) were [in testing](https://www.theverge.com/tech/938500/facebook-whatsapp-instagram-meta-ai-subscriptions) earlier this year, but are now available globally starting today, with several tiers for individual users, creators, and businesses. Meta says the "core experience" on its apps and Meta AI will still be free, and users can still get its subscriptions for Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp without a bundle. It also says it plans to expand the bundles to include "Edits, AI glasses, and more over time."
